Prepares output for HDX-MS for the deuteration uptake or percent deuteration for the time points.

Source: R/output_tp_def.R
output_tp.Rd

Returns a data frame organized for additional analysis. In columns are deuteration uptake or percent deuteration data for the given protein states. Function allows for writing csv with data, matching sequences of peptide. Protein.States, Deut.times, or number of replicates can be specified.

Usage

output_tp(
  filepath,
  replicates,
  states,
  times,
  seq_match = FALSE,
  csv = "NA",
  percent = FALSE,
  min_replicates = 2,
  .arg_df = NULL
)

Arguments

filepath

filepath to the input file. Input file is All_results table from HDX_Examiner, where all the fields are marked for export. Can also be a DynamX cluster/state export, or a table from read_hdx() / as_hdx_long().

replicates

optional maximum number of replicates per state and time. By default every replicate is used, so states may have different numbers of replicates (e.g. 3 and 4); missing measurements are NA. Replicates are numbered in the order their experiments appear in the file.

states

function allows to choose what states should be used for analysis. Default all states are used.

times

lists the deuteration times to be used in analysis. Default all states used.

seq_match

How peptides are matched between states. FALSE (default): a peptide is kept only if the same Sequence, Start, End and Charge are found in every state (exact sequence identity). TRUE: peptides are matched by position only (Start, End and Charge), ignoring Sequence, so peptides covering e.g. a point mutation are kept; where the sequences differ between states they are joined with "." in the Sequence column.

csv

Flag allowing saving the output as csv. With default csv="NA", data is not saved. If csv output is desided, provide output name.

percent

What the values are. FALSE (default): deuterium uptake in Da. TRUE: percent deuteration as reported by the input (HDXExaminer's Deut %, i.e. relative to the theoretical maximum; for DynamX 100 x uptake / MaxUptake). "FD": percent of the measured fully deuterated control, 100 x uptake / FD uptake of the same peptide and state (FD replicates averaged, charge states pooled); this corrects for back-exchange and D2O content. Peptides without a usable FD value (missing, or FD uptake <= 0) keep their row with empty (NA) values. "per_residue": uptake per exchangeable amide, Da / nb_exch_deut() (length - 2 - prolines after the first residue), so peptide length does not affect the critical-interval half of the significance rule (TRUE and "FD" are length-normalized too). The p-values are the same on every scale; only the critical interval and the differences change.

min_replicates

a peptide is kept only if it has at least this many replicate values in every state at that time. Default 2, the minimum for a standard deviation and a t-test.

.arg_df

advanced/internal: a pre-computed arg_df() data.frame for this same filepath, to skip re-reading and re-parsing the file from disk. Default NULL reads filepath as usual - only pass this when calling output_tp() many times for the same file (e.g. once per pair of states) and arg_df(filepath) has already been computed once by the caller; passing a data.frame that doesn't match filepath will silently produce wrong results, since nothing here re-checks it.

Value

data frame with reorganized data where in columns is the deuteration uptake for Protein States. Attributes "replicates" (number of replicate columns per state), "states", "times" and "percent" record how it was built.

Examples

file_nm<-system.file("extdata", "All_results_table.csv", package = "HDXBoxeR")
a<- output_tp(filepath=file_nm) ###all default parameters used
#> Protein.States used: Unbound bound
#> Deut.times used: 3.00s 60.00s 1800.00s 72000.00s
#> 29 peptide row(s) dropped: 29 not measured in every state, 0 with fewer than 2 replicate value(s)
#> Number of replicates used: Unbound=3 bound=3
#> no csv file written


# all possible flags listed & percent deuteration output,
# with sequences matching for protein states.

a<-output_tp(filepath=file_nm, replicates=3, states=c("bound", "Unbound"),
times=c("3.00s", "72000.00s"), seq_match=TRUE, csv="NA", percent=TRUE)
#> 14 peptide row(s) dropped: 14 not measured in every state, 0 with fewer than 2 replicate value(s)
#> Number of replicates used: bound=3 Unbound=3
#> no csv file written
